questions.title: What sentence will Egyptian television presenter Sarah Khalifa receive at trial in her drug-trafficking case?
questions.background: Sarah Khalifa was arrested in Egypt in April 2025 as part of a drug investigation.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The trial court’s announced judgment in the drug-trafficking prosecution stemming from Khalifa’s April 2025 arrest, as confirmed by official court information or reliable reporting from Al-Ahram. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the trial court announces its verdict and sentence. Later appellate decisions and judgments in unrelated cases do not count. Accepted Answer Format : Provide a short legal term identifying the principal penalty imposed, or the court’s disposition if no penalty is imposed. If multiple penalties are imposed, report the most severe.
questions.current_reasoning: Sarah Khalifa and 27 co-defendants are on trial before the New Cairo Criminal Court for forming a transnational gang importing precursors from China and manufacturing over 750 kg of synthetic narcotics, plus unlicensed firearms; on June 11-12, 2026, Egypt's Public Prosecution formally demanded the maximum statutory penalty of execution by hanging while the court reviewed forensic reports ahead of a verdict. Under Article 33 of Egypt's Narcotics Law (and Al-Ahram's reporting), large-scale narcotics importation and manufacturing carries either life imprisonment (25 years) or the death penalty. In Egyptian judicial practice, prosecutors routinely request execution in major felony trials, but criminal courts more frequently impose life imprisonment—especially for female defendants who are not the primary fugitive ringleaders—while death penalty (which would align with a ~6-week Grand Mufti referral timeline into early August), aggravated imprisonment (via Art. 17 discretion), acquittal, and simple imprisonment cover almost the entire disposition space.
